body.input: Which companies expanded to Finland in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available information, a number of companies have had or expanded their operational presence in Finland in 2026. Here are some notable examples:

## Notable Expansions / New Entries into Finland in 2026

- **Heitman (US)** — Launched **Talli**, a Nordic drive-up self-storage platform, after acquiring a majority stake in Finnish developer Talliosake. The platform started with 11 properties in Finland and 4 in Sweden, with plans for further expansion across both countries.

- **WEG S.A. (Brazil)** — Expanded its Nordic operations by opening a **new office in Finland** in January 2026, strengthening its presence in the region.

- **Kesko (Finland)** — Announced the acquisition of Saint-Gobain's building distribution business in Finland (completed November 2026), significantly expanding its building and technical trade segment.

## Companies with Established Operational Presence in Finland (as of 2026)

Many major multinational companies maintain operations in Finland, including Tesla, Intel, BAE Systems, Dell Technologies, Nike, Procter & Gamble, PepsiCo, FedEx, Cognizant, Booking Holdings, Caterpillar, Abbott Laboratories, Rio Tinto, Cellnex Telecom, Marsh & McLennan, Aon, and many others.

## Broader Investment Climate

Finland's startup ecosystem also showed renewed strength in 2026, with venture capital investment reaching €765 million in 2025 (up 60%), of which €494 million came from foreign investors. Three Finnish startups listed on the Helsinki Stock Exchange in 2026 with a combined market capitalization of nearly €6 billion. Finland also signed a Memorandum of Understanding with California in September 2026 to strengthen commercial and economic ties.

*Note: A comprehensive list of every company that expanded to Finland in 2026 is not available from a single source. The examples above reflect specific expansion announcements identified in recent reporting.*

Talli will be led by Talliosake’s existing management team, with Talliosake retaining a minority stake in the business. Since 2010, the Finnish company has delivered more than 6,400 drive-up self-storage units across 230 properties in Finland and Sweden.  
  
The partnership marks a shift in Talliosake’s business model, which has traditionally focused on developing and selling individual self-storage units. Talli will instead adopt a develop-to-hold strategy, developing and operating income-generating properties for long-term ownership.

In brief

Venture capital in Finland is funded by domestic and foreign investors: EUR 765 million went into Finnish companies in 2025, up 60%. Early-stage funds whose own pages state a stage include OpenOcean, Maki.vc, Icebreaker.vc, Inventure, Butterfly Ventures, Vendep Capital and Kvanted, alongside Tesi. This page compares their stage, ticket and focus.

## Key takeaways [...] EUR 494M foreign, EUR 270M domesticVenture capital in Finnish startups in 2025 from foreign investors (up 97%) and domestic investors (up 19%, a record)Source: Venture capital Suomessa 2025, Pääomasijoittajat ry (Finnish-language PDF), Apr 2026

The figures come from the association's report on 2025, published on 8 Apr 2026. The report is in Finnish only, and the English wording here is ours1. The association's statistics page lists it with that date2. [...] ## Key takeaways

 Venture capital investment in Finnish companies reached EUR 765 million in 2025, up 60%, while the number of companies receiving it fell 14%.
 Foreign investors put in EUR 494 million and domestic investors EUR 270 million in 2025.
 Stated first tickets range from about EUR 0.3 million on average at Butterfly Ventures to EUR 2-10 million for Tesi's direct venture investments.
 Most funds name their own route for founders: an email address, a form or an apply page, linked in the table.
 Lifeline Ventures and Voima Ventures are left out because their official pages could not be read on 7 Oct 2026.

# Finland’s startup ecosystem strengthens as the number of new startups returns to growth

Release 13.11.2026

The number of identified startups in Finland returned to growth in 2024 after several years of decline. A total of 331 new startups were identified, compared with 258 in 2023, representing an increase of approximately 28%. [...] A startup is a young, innovative company aiming for international growth, whose business model and market are often still developing. Startups differ from other new companies particularly in their focus on scalable business models and their need for external funding.

The turnaround is encouraging, although the number of startups has declined over the longer term. In 2016, 587 startups were identified.

Identified startups by year of establishment

Startups that received funding from Business Finland or angel investment from FiBAN, or participated in Slush (2014–2026), by year of establishment. The number of startups established in 2025 in particular will be updated as more companies are identified and newly established companies receive funding or participate in Slush. [...] Two out of three projects have a strong focus on digital solutions and the use of artificial intelligence and data analytics. Health and well-being solutions, as well as solutions related to defence and security, also feature prominently among the funded projects.

“These projects provide a strong foundation for developing solutions that improve productivity and renew Finland’s business landscape. Startups can bring new products, services and industries to Finnish exports and open up new markets,” says Ilmari.
